message.content:
This appears to come from a CBP ruling on hydraulic hose crimp fittings. Candidates are heading 7307 (tube or pipe fittings of iron or steel) and heading 8412 (parts of engines and motors).

Heading 7307 covers fittings for tubes or pipes, and zinc-plated carbon steel crimp fittings are not stainless. Subheading 7307.91 covers flanges, 7307.92 threaded elbows, bends and sleeves, 7307.93 butt welding fittings, and 7307.99 other. The note that "none will feature dedicated pipe or tube connections" suggests the fittings may be excluded from 7307 and classified as parts of hydraulic engines or motors under 8412.90. Note also that heading 7307 covers fittings for tubes and pipes, whereas hoses fall under 3917 or 4009, and hose fittings are generally classified under 7307.

Several CBP rulings on hose fittings, such as NY N301717, put crimp fittings in 7307.99.5045. The phrase "None will feature dedicated pipe or tube connections" resembles a ruling in which the fittings were classified in 8481.90 as parts of valves, or in 8412.90. However, hose couplings for hydraulic hoses are generally classified in 7307.99. For threaded fittings the likely choice is 7307.92.30 (threaded elbows, bends and sleeves), but the straight and non-threaded crimp sleeves make 7307.99 more likely.

Section XV Note 2 defines "parts of general use" to include articles of heading 7307. Because these are parts of general use, they are excluded from Section XVI (which includes 8412), so 7307 applies. Within 7307.99, the zinc-plated carbon steel fittings would go to 7307.99.5045 (other, other, other).
